why: The truth puts material bought over the quoted material at $3,029,316 in 2021 (by year bought), $728,185 in 2022 and $769,433 in 2018, with 2019-20 and 2023-24 under quote (-$505,497 in 2023, -$346,047 in 2024) (t399). The finding's 2021 shortfall of $2,913,379, its small 2022 figure and its recovery from 2023 match this, and so does its mechanism: repeat-part prices held at the old level while steel was bought at higher prices, with the surcharge recovering only a little. It misses the smaller 2018 episode, and its $1.09M-a-year size is lower than the truth's average of about $1.88M a year over 2021-22, but the effect, timing and cause are right.
